Sam: heads up — CI started failing flaky on the quantized model rollouts after yesterday's change. failing step: eval-harness/runner:batch_worker
Rick: saw a few of those, errors look like timeouts + worker backlog. example log:
```
[2026-02-12 09:12:11] worker-23 ERROR eval_runner: shard(7) timeout after 30s while waiting for batch
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/eval_runner/runner.py", line 412, in process_batch
    result = model.infer(batch)
TimeoutError: inference timeout
```
```
ci-bot: pipeline:master #4821 failed — see /ci/logs/4821
```
Shiv: we switched to int8 quant + dynamic batching yesterday. suspect: quantized models are slower on longer sequences and our per-shard timeouts assume fp16 numbers
Taylor: also noticed weird metric jitter: some CI runs report accuracy stepping down 2-3% then back up next run. could be partial aggregation bug.
Maja: pinged infra earlier — memory on workers spiked when batch sizes hit 32, OOMs were rare but GC made latencies worse.
Sam: sequence: enable quant -> pipeline increased max_batch_size to 32 -> shard scheduler kept packing -> some workers got big batches for long sequences -> timeouts
Rick: what if we add a simple backpressure: cap effective batch size based on median seq length statistics per-shard? quick fix: token-aware batch cap
Shiv: agree. quick mitigation: set max_batch_tokens = min(4096, floor(4096 / median_seq_len)) per worker. also increase shard timeout to 60s while we validate.
Taylor: still worried about metric jitter. I dug into the CI aggregator: if a worker fails mid-shard we write partial metrics and then avg across shards without weighting -> can shift the reported metric when one heavy shard fails earlier.
Maja: that sounds like a bug — aggregator should ignore shards that returned errors or at least mark run flaky.
Sam: propose immediate steps:
  1) revert max_batch_size to 16 in CI config
  2) add token-aware cap to scheduler (fallback to 8/16)
  3) bump shard timeout to 60s in CI
  4) change aggregator to skip shards with non-zero error_count
Rick: I'll make a small PR for 1+3. patch:
```
--- a/ci/pipelines/eval.yml
+++ b/ci/pipelines/eval.yml
@@
-    env:
-      MAX_BATCH_SIZE: 32
+    env:
+      MAX_BATCH_SIZE: 16
+      SHARD_TIMEOUT_S: 60
```
Shiv: I'll add token-aware cap to the scheduler (quick hack) — patch snippet:
```
# scheduler.py
def effective_batch_size(worker_stats):
    median_len = worker_stats.median_seq_len or 32
    return max(1, min(config.MAX_BATCH_SIZE, config.MAX_BATCH_TOKENS // median_len))
```
Taylor: for aggregator, here's offending code in ci/metrics/aggregate.py:
```
# currently
avg_acc = sum(shard.acc for shard in shards) / len(shards)
# should be weighted and skip errors
```
Maja: I'll open an issue to add dashboard alerts for shard-error-rate > 5% and avg_batch_tokens > threshold. ops-bot can we get an alert rule?
ops-bot: creating alert 'eval_runner:shard_error_rate' with threshold 0.05 -> channel #eng-ml-alerts
Sam: thanks. timeline: Rick -> PR in next 15m, Shiv -> scheduler change + unit tests by EOD, Taylor -> aggregator fix + CI test, Maja -> alert + dashboard widget.
Rick: PR up: https://git.redwood/ci/pipelines/pull/289
Shiv: scheduler small change pushed to my branch, running unit tests locally. concern: need to ensure token stats are per-shard not per-run.
Taylor: added aggregator unit tests to cover partial-failure weighting. found second bug: we were truncating float metrics to two decimals when storing, which amplifies noise — pushing fix.
Maja: dashboard: added 'p95 batch time by shard' and 'shard error rate' widgets. linked to the new alert.
Sam: re-run CI after Rick's revert -> https://ci.redwood/run/4822 started
ci-bot: run 4822: eval pipeline started
Rick: run 4822 succeeded on first pass, but one run had a p95 batch time spike to 48s on shard 12 — still high but no timeouts. looks better.
Taylor: aggregator now skips error shards and weights by processed_samples; reported accuracy stabilized across 3 runs.
Shiv: next: validate with longer sequences in stress test (seq_len up to 2048). I'll spin up a dedicated test with 1000 shards.
Maja: we'll keep alerting enabled for 24h, collect traces for any shard with p95_batch_time > 40s.
Sam: postmortem notes: root cause = token-unaware batching + quant slower tail on long sequences. fixes: token-aware cap, revert batch size, aggregator robustness, longer shard timeout, dashboard alerts.
Rick: follow-up: we should also add model performance profiles to model catalog so CI knows expected p95 latencies for quantized variants before enabling wide rollout.
Sam: agreed — action item for model-onboarding checklist.
Taylor: cool — closing this thread after monitoring window. thanks all :thumbsup:
ci-bot: closing run 4822 after 1h monitoring — no regressions detected.
